questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 6: How Migrating Birds Recalibrate Direction
Three students discuss how migrating birds correct their direction after several cloudy days.

Student 1: Birds rely mainly on the position of the setting sun. A clear sunset after cloudy weather allows them to reset an internal compass for the next day.

Student 2: Birds rely mainly on Earth’s magnetic field. Cloud cover has little effect on the compass itself; errors arise when local magnetic conditions are disturbed.

Student 3: Birds use both cues. Magnetic information provides a continuous reference, while sunset information can recalibrate how that magnetic reference is interpreted at a particular location.

Which investigation would best distinguish the proposed explanations?
F) Ask one observer which explanation sounds most familiar.
G) Measure only the final outcome without varying or comparing any relevant factor.
H) Independently manipulate sunset visibility and magnetic field direction in a controlled orientation arena.
J) Remove all records of the procedures before interpreting the results.

options.A: Ask one observer which explanation sounds most familiar.
options.B: Measure only the final outcome without varying or comparing any relevant factor.
options.C: Independently manipulate sunset visibility and magnetic field direction in a controlled orientation arena.
options.D: Remove all records of the procedures before interpreting the results.

questions.explanation: The proposed test measures variables that differ among the explanations.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE MATERIAL SET 5
Students tested how water temperature affected the time required for a tablet to dissolve. They used identical tablets, 104 mL of water in each cup, and stirred each cup at the same rate.

TABLE 1
Temperature (°C) | Dissolving time (s)
10 | 33
20 | 25
30 | 20
40 | 16

Trial 2 repeated the procedure with twice the water volume. Researcher 1 claims that higher temperature increases particle motion and therefore decreases dissolving time. Researcher 2 agrees that temperature matters but claims that stirring rate is the dominant factor whenever stirring is not controlled.

Which hypothesis is directly tested?
A) Tablets always dissolve faster in larger cups.
B) All chemical reactions require light.
C) The tablet changes the mass of the cup.
D) Increasing water temperature decreases tablet dissolving time.

options.A: Tablets always dissolve faster in larger cups.
options.B: All chemical reactions require light.
options.C: The tablet changes the mass of the cup.
options.D: Increasing water temperature decreases tablet dissolving time.

questions.explanation: The keyed response follows the material and directly targets 识别研究问题或可检验假设.

Students tested how water temperature affected the time required for a tablet to dissolve. They used identical tablets, 129 mL of water in each cup, and stirred each cup at the same rate.

TABLE 1
Temperature (°C) | Dissolving time (s)
10 | 33
20 | 25
30 | 20
40 | 16

Trial 2 repeated the procedure with twice the water volume. Researcher 1 claims that higher temperature increases particle motion and therefore decreases dissolving time. Researcher 2 agrees that temperature matters but claims that stirring rate is the dominant factor whenever stirring is not controlled.

Which hypothesis is directly tested?
A) Tablets always dissolve faster in larger cups.
B) Increasing water temperature decreases tablet dissolving time.
C) All chemical reactions require light.
D) The tablet changes the mass of the cup.

options.A: Tablets always dissolve faster in larger cups.
options.B: Increasing water temperature decreases tablet dissolving time.
options.C: All chemical reactions require light.
options.D: The tablet changes the mass of the cup.

questions.explanation: The keyed response follows the material and directly targets 识别研究问题或可检验假设.
